backward_compat_traps.rule: A component must support all data rates up to its advertised maximum (e.g. 4/8/12 for a 12G device).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Assuming a high-rate device can only run at its top rate breaks interop with a lower-rate partner; negotiation lands at the highest common rate.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Standard (16-lane module, 100-130 um pitch, <=25 mm) and Advanced (64-lane module, 25-55 um pitch, <=2 mm) have different bump-outs.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Standard and Advanced bump-outs are not interchangeable; the package class is a hardware property, not a runtime mode.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Raw Mode bypasses the D2D Adapter's Flit/CRC/Retry.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Relying on UCIe for integrity in Raw Mode is wrong — the carried protocol must supply its own reliability.

backward_compat_traps.rule: The 800 MHz sideband (2 lanes/direction) is always-on and carries no mainband data.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Treating the sideband as part of the data path, or assuming it can be powered down, breaks management/register access.

backward_compat_traps.rule: UCIe mainband is source-synchronous (forwarded Track/clock), not clock-data-recovery; the mainband is unencoded.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Designing for an embedded-clock 8b/10b or 128b/130b line code (as in PCIe/USB SerDes) is wrong for the UCIe die-to-die PHY.

backward_compat_traps.rule: Both ends must agree on the Flit format (64B / 256B / 256B latency-optimized).
backward_compat_traps.trap: A 256B-only partner cannot interoperate with a 64B-only partner without a common format.

fields.spec_version: Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) Specification Revision 1.1 (2023)
previous_versions: UCIe 1.0 (2022) — initial release: three-layer D2D stack (PHY + D2D Adapter + Protocol Layer), Standard + Advanced Packages, 4-32 GT/s, FDI/RDI, 64B Flit, PCIe/CXL/Streaming, sideband.

key_changes.summary: Incremental revision over UCIe 1.0: clarifications and errata, configuration-register / compliance / RDI-FDI interface improvements, and reliability / automotive-grade enhancements. The layered architecture (PHY / D2D Adapter / Protocol Layer), package classes (Standard / Advanced), data rates (4-32 GT/s), module model (16/64-lane, 1/2/4 modules), Flit/CRC/Retry, sideband, and PCIe/CXL/Streaming mappings are carried forward unchanged.

future_versions_industry_outline.summary: Adds a standardized manageability/system architecture and 3D packaging (vertical die stacking) support, with further compliance and DFx enhancements; same three-layer foundation.

fields.version_naming_history_note: UCIe is maintained by the UCIe Consortium (120+ member companies). UCIe 1.0 (2022) established the open die-to-die chiplet interconnect; UCIe 1.1 (2023) is an incremental revision adding errata, compliance/register/interface improvements, and reliability/automotive enhancements. Facts here are grounded in the public UCIe Consortium tutorial overview (Hot Chips 2023) and the UCIe 1.x specification structure (three layers, Standard/Advanced Packages, 4-32 GT/s, FDI/RDI, Flit/CRC/Retry, sideband, PCIe/CXL/Streaming mappings).
